   Norwalk Community Facilities Financing Authority Agenda Report
  June 18, 2019

TO:  Honorable Norwalk Facilities Financing Authority Commission

FROM:  Jesus M. Gomez, Chief Administrative Officer

BY:  Jana Stuard, Treasurer
  Christine Roberto, Public Services Manager

SUBJECT:  RESOLUTION NO. NCFFA-23 - STREET IMPROVEMENTS FINANCING
  – NORWALK COMMUNITY FACILITIES FINANCING AUTHORITY

Background:

In July 2008, Los Angeles County Metro’s Measure R was approved by Los Angeles
County voters. In November 2016, Metro’s Measure M was approved. Both Measure R
and Measure M included a new half-cent sales tax creating an ongoing source of funding
for mobility improvements across Los Angeles County. Under Measure R and M, major
road, transit and walking/biking projects are slated to be built in the next 40 years.
Measure R and Measure M also includes funds that are returned directly to local cities for
their own transportation projects and annual funding to ensure infrastructure is
maintained.

The City has developed a Local Streets Rehabilitation Program that identifies quadrants
of the City where road repairs will be undertaken with Measure M funding and with
Measure R funding. These projects (Projects) qualify for funding under Metro’s guidelines
for both Measure R and Measure M. The staff has identified the Projects to be undertaken
in the first 2 years by Zone, corresponding to the Zones identified on the Local Streets
Rehabilitation Program map. The estimated cost of the Projects by Zone is shown below.

  Zone  Cost  Year  Measure M  Measure R
  Zone 24  $ 2,444,100  Year 1  $ 2,444,100 $  -
  Zone 27  4,407,700  Year 1  -  4,407,700
  Zone 32  3,154,400  Year 1  -  3,154,400
  Misc  765,400  Year 1  765,400  -
  Zone 3  4,896,400  Year 2  4,896,400  -
  Zone 8  2,996,600  Year 2  -  2,996,600
  Zone 19  3,644,200  Year 2  3,644,200  -
  $22,308,800  $11,750,100 $10,558,700
 Resolution No. NCFFA-23 - Norwalk Community Facilities  June 18, 2019
Financing Authority - Street Improvements Financing  Page No. 2

In the twelve months between January and December 2018, the City received a total of
$2.4 million in combined Measure R and Measure M sales tax. In addition to using the
annual funds to fund the Projects on a pay-as-you-go basis or to accumulate funds to
finance the Projects, the City has the opportunity to leverage the Measure R and Measure
M Revenues. The City can currently raise funds for Project costs through the issuance
of Measure R Revenue Bonds and Measure M Revenue Bonds (Bonds), providing
enough funds to undertake the Projects with a pledge of 65% of revenue received.
Repayment of the Bonds will take place over fifteen years, which is the estimated useful
life of the Projects financed.

On March 19, 2019, the City Council authorized contracts with Norton Rose Fulbright to
act as Bond Counsel, Harrell & Company Advisors to act as Municipal Advisor and Stifel
Nicolaus & Company to serve as underwriter for the Bonds.

The Bonds are expected to be issued in early July to coincide with the first phase of street
construction in July and August. The Bonds will be issued by the Norwalk Community
Facilities Financing Authority (Authority) and secured by pledge agreements between the
City and the Authority, pledging the Measure R and Measure M sales tax to repay the
Bonds. In order to meet a July issuance schedule, certain resolutions approving the
indentures and pledge agreements were required to be adopted at least 60 days prior to
the sale of the Bonds. On May 7, 2019, the City Council and the Authority Commission
adopted resolutions approving the indentures and pledge agreements and authorizing a
total amount of Bonds up to $25 million.

The final step in the approval process is for the City Council and the Authority Commission
to approve documents related to the sale of the Bonds.

Financing Approvals:

By adopting the proposed resolution, the City Council will approve the form of the
following documents in connection with the financing:

    Preliminary Official Statement;
    Bond Purchase Agreement between the City, the Authority and the Underwriter;
  and
    Continuing Disclosure Agreement.

By adopting the proposed resolution, the Authority Commission will approve the form of
the following documents in connection with the financing:
   Preliminary Official Statement; and
   Bond Purchase Agreement between the City, the Authority and the Underwriter.

Both resolutions authorize the City Manager/Authority Chief Administrative Officer and
Finance Director/Authority Treasurer to execute the documents for the sale of the Bonds
 Resolution No. NCFFA-23 - Norwalk Community Facilities  June 18, 2019
Financing Authority - Street Improvements Financing  Page No. 3

within certain parameters. The underwriter’s discount shall not greater than 1% of the par
amount of the Bonds and net true interest cost shall not be greater than 3.5%. The final
maturity of the Bonds shall not exceed June 1, 2034.

Fiscal Impact:

The Measure R Revenue Bonds and Measure M Revenues Bonds will be secured by
future Measure R sales tax revenues and Measure M sales tax revenues allocated to the
City annually by the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority. No
money in the General Fund will be used to pay debt service on the Bonds.

The staff expects to use approximately 65% of the annual Measure R and Measure M
revenue to pay debt service, with the remaining revenues used for pay-as-you-go
projects. The annual debt service for the Measure M Bonds is estimated at $975,000 and
the annual debt service for the Measure R Bonds is estimated at $865,000, payable for
15 years.

In May, the estimated interest rate on the Bonds was 3.05%. Due to fears about the
economic impact of tariffs and heightened expectations that the Federal Reserve may in
fact lower the fed funds rate, as of May 31 the estimated interest rate was 2.55%. Market
conditions will continue to change, and the interest rate won’t be locked in until July 11.

If interest rates are at these current levels when the Bonds are sold, the expected par
(principal) amount of the Bonds, allocated costs to each series and net proceeds for Street
Improvements is shown below. In early May, the net proceeds were approximately
$700,000 less than the total estimated Project costs. As of May 31, 2019, the bonding
capacity is sufficient to fund the expected Project costs.

  Measure M  Measure R  Total
 Street Improvement Project Funds  $11,750,100 $10,558,700 $22,308,800
 Costs  244,900  216,300  461,200
 Total  11,995,000 10,775,000 22,770,000
 Original Issue Premium  (1,965,000) (1,760,000) (3,725,000)
 Bond Amount  10,030,000  9,015,000 19,045,000

An original issue premium is generated when investors want to hedge against rising
interest rates and require a high stated interest rate (such as 5.0%), but price the bonds
to yield a lower current market interest rate (such as 2.0%) and therefore pay the City
more than 100% of the face value of the bonds. The par amount of the Bonds and the
amount of the original issue premium will be subject to prevailing market conditions at the
time of sale.

The costs to issue the Bonds will be paid for from Bond proceeds. The costs are
estimated as follows:

Citizens Advised: N/A

Strategic Action Plan Implementation:

The recommended action will further the City’s goal of: (6.D.5) Enhance access and
maintain compliance of public rights or way and City Facilities.

Recommended Action:

Staff recommends the Norwalk Community Facilities Financing Authority adopt
Resolution No. NCFFA-23, A RESOLUTION OF THE NORWALK COMMUNITY
FACILITIES FINANCING AUTHORITY APPROVING A BOND PURCHASE
AGREEMENT AND A PRELIMINARY OFFICIAL STATEMENT; AND AUTHORIZING
AND DIRECTING CERTAIN ACTIONS WITH RESPECT THERETO.

   RESOLUTION NO. NCFFA-23

  A RESOLUTION OF THE NORWALK COMMUNITY FACILITIES
  FINANCING AUTHORITY APPROVING A BOND PURCHASE
  AGREEMENT AND A PRELIMINARY OFFICIAL STATEMENT; AND
  AUTHORIZING AND DIRECTING CERTAIN ACTIONS WITH RESPECT
  THERETO

  WHEREAS, the Norwalk Community Facilities Financing Authority (the “Authority”)
is a joint powers authority duly organized and existing under and pursuant to that certain
Joint Exercise of Powers Agreement, dated as of August 1, 1989, as amended from time
to time, by and between the City of Norwalk (the “City”) and the Norwalk Parking Authority,
and under the provisions of Articles 1 through 4 (commencing with Section 6500) of
Chapter 5 of Division 7 of Title 1 of the Government Code of the State of California (the
“Act”), and is authorized pursuant to Article 4 of the Act (the “Bond Law”) to, among other
purposes, borrow money for the purpose of financing the capital improvement needs of
the City; and

  WHEREAS, the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority
(“LACMTA”) is authorized by Sections 130350.4 and 130350.5 of the California Public
Utilities Code to impose a retail transactions and use tax at a rate of 0.5 percent that is
applicable in the incorporated and unincorporated areas of the County of Los Angeles,
California (the “County”) if authorized by at least two-thirds of the electors voting on the
issue; and

  WHEREAS, in accordance with such provision, LACMTA, on July 24, 2008,
adopted Ordinance No. 08-01, known as the Traffic Relief and Rail Expansion Ordinance,
Imposing a Transactions and Use Tax to be Administered by the State Board of
Equalization (the “Measure R Ordinance”), imposing the transactions and use tax for a
period of 30 years, and the Ordinance was submitted to the electors of the County in the
form of Measure R and approved by greater than a two-thirds vote at an election held on
November 4, 2008; and

  WHEREAS, the Measure R Ordinance, as so approved, imposed for a period of
30 years, beginning July 1, 2009, a tax upon the sale of tangible personal property at
retail at a rate of 1/2 of 1% of the gross receipts of the sale and a complementary tax
upon the storage, use or other consumption in the County at a rate of 1/2 of 1% of the
sales price of the property whose storage, use or other consumption is subject to the tax
(the “Measure R Sales Tax”); and

  WHEREAS, LACMTA is authorized by Section 130350.7 of the California Public
Utilities Code to impose a retail transactions and use tax that is applicable in the County,
at a rate that, when combined with the Measure R Sales Tax during any period when the
Measure R Sales Tax is in effect and upon expiration of the Measure R Sales Tax, shall
not exceed one percent, if authorized by at least two-thirds of the electors voting on the
issue; and
   WHEREAS, in accordance with such provision, the LACMTA, on July 23, 2016,
adopted Ordinance No. 16-01, known as the Los Angeles County Traffic Improvement
Plan (the “Measure M Ordinance”), imposing a transactions and use tax for transportation
purposes subject to approval by the electors of the County; and

  WHEREAS, the Measure M Ordinance was submitted to the electors of the County
in the form of Measure M and approved by greater than a two-thirds vote at an election
held on November 8, 2016; and

  WHEREAS, the Measure M Ordinance, as so approved, imposes a tax, beginning
July 1, 2017, upon the sale of tangible personal property at retail at a rate of 1/2 of 1% of
the gross receipts of the sale and a complementary tax upon the storage, use or other
consumption in the County at a rate of 1/2 of 1% of the sales price of the property whose
storage, use or other consumption is subject to the tax, with the rate increasing to 1% on
July 1, 2039 (the “Measure M Sales Tax”); and

  WHEREAS, a portion of the Measure R Sales Tax revenues are allocated and paid
(the “Measure R Receipts”) by LACMTA to the cities located within the County (the “Local
Agencies”), including the City, and to the County for the purpose of funding transportation
projects (the “Measure R Projects”) eligible to be funded with Measure R Receipts
pursuant to the Measure R Ordinance and the guidelines prepared by LACMTA and
disseminated to the Local Agencies, approved by the LACMTA Board on October 24,
2009, relating to the administration and use of the Measure R Sales Tax and the Measure
R Receipts; and

  WHEREAS, a portion of the Measure M Sales Tax revenues are allocated and
paid (the “Measure M Receipts”) by LACMTA to the Local Agencies, including the City,
and to the County for the purpose of funding transportation projects (the “Measure M
Projects”) eligible to be funded with Measure M Receipts pursuant to the Measure M
Ordinance and the guidelines prepared by LACMTA and disseminated to the Local
Agencies, approved by the LACMTA Board on March 1, 2018, relating to the
administration and use of the Measure M Sales Tax and the Measure M Receipts; and

  WHEREAS, the Authority has determined to issue and deliver at the request of,
and for the benefit of, the City, a series of bonds payable from the City’s Measure M
Receipts, entitled “Norwalk Community Facilities Financing Authority Sales Tax Revenue
Bonds (Limited Tax Bonds) (Measure M), Series 2019A” (the “2019A Bonds”) with such
subseries designations and other additions and modifications as may be appropriate to
finance (i) the payment of the costs of the Measure M Projects, including the
reimbursement of the City for certain amounts expended on the Measure M Projects prior
to the issuance of the 2019A Bonds, (ii) a bond reserve fund for the 2019A Bonds, if
necessary or desirable, and (iii) the costs of issuance incurred in connection with the
2019A Bonds; and

  WHEREAS, the Authority has determined to issue and deliver at the request of,
and for the benefit of the City, a series of bonds payable from the City’s Measure R
Receipts, entitled “Norwalk Community Facilities Financing Authority Sales Tax Revenue

Resolution No. NCFFA-23  Page 2 of 5
 Bonds (Limited Tax Bonds) (Measure R), Series 2019B” (the “2019B Bonds” and,
together with the 2019A Bonds, the “Bonds”) with such subseries designations and other
additions and modifications as may be appropriate, to finance (i) the payment of the costs
of the Measure R Projects, including the reimbursement of the City for certain amounts
expended on the Measure R Projects prior to the issuance of the 2019B Bonds, (ii) a bond
reserve fund for the 2019B Bonds, if necessary or desirable, and (iii) the costs of
issuance incurred in connection with the 2019B Bonds; and

  WHEREAS, on May 7, 2019, the Authority adopted Resolution No. NCFFA-22 to
approve the issuance of the Bonds and matters in connection therewith; and

  WHEREAS, Stifel, Nicolaus & Company, Incorporated, as underwriter for the
Bonds, has presented to the City and the Authority the form of a Bond Purchase
Agreement (the “Bond Purchase Agreement”), which will set forth the terms of sale of the
Bonds; and

  WHEREAS, to provide information about the Bonds, the Authority will prepare a
Preliminary Official Statement (the “Preliminary Official Statement”) and a final Official
Statement (the “Official Statement”).

  NOW THEREFORE, THE NORWALK COMMUNITY FACILITIES FINANCING
AUTHORITY RESOLVES:

  Section 1. The Authority hereby approves the Bond Purchase Agreement
relating to the Bonds, substantially in the form on file with the Secretary of the Authority,
with such revisions, amendments and completions as shall be approved by the President
of the Authority (or in the President’s absence, the Vice President), the Chief
Administrative Officer of the Authority and the Treasurer of the Authority (each, an
“Authorized Officer”) with the advice of counsel to the Authority, such approval to be
conclusively evidenced by the execution and delivery thereof. The Bond Purchase
Agreement shall provide for an underwriter’s discount of not greater than 1.0% and net
true interest cost of not greater than 3.5%. The final maturity of the 2019A Bonds shall
not exceed 2034 and the final maturity of the 2019B Bonds shall not exceed 2034.

  Section 2. The Authority hereby approves the Preliminary Official Statement
relating to the Bonds, substantially in the form on file with the Secretary of the Authority,
with such revisions, amendments and completions as shall be approved by an Authorized
Officer with the advice of counsel to the Authority in order to make the Preliminary Official
Statement final as of its date, except for the omission of certain information, as permitted
by Section 240.15c2-12(b)(1) of Title 17 of the Code of Federal Regulations (“Rule 15c2-
12”), and any certificate relating to the finality of the Official Statement under Rule 15c2-
12. An Authorized Officer is authorized and directed to execute and deliver the Official
Statement in substantially the form hereby approved, with such additions and changes as
may be approved by counsel and the Authorized Officer executing the same, such
approval to be conclusively evidenced by the execution and delivery thereof.

   Section 3. Each Authorized Officer and other officers of the Authority are hereby
authorized and directed, for and in the name and on behalf of the Authority, to do any and
all things and take any and all actions, including procurement of a municipal bond
insurance policy, if any, and execution and delivery of any and all assignments,
certificates, requisitions, agreements, notices, consents, instruments of conveyance,
warrants and other documents, which they, or any of them, deem necessary or advisable
to consummate the lawful issuance and sale of the Bonds and the consummation of the
transactions as described herein.

  Section 4. All approvals, consents, directions, notices, orders, requests and
other actions permitted or required by any of the documents authorized by this Resolution,
whether before or after the issuance of the Bonds, including, without limitation, any of the
foregoing that may be necessary or desirable in connection with any investment of
proceeds of the Bonds, or any agreements with paying agents or the Trustee or any
similar action may be given or taken by any Authorized Officer without further
authorization or direction by the Authority, and each Authorized Officer is hereby
authorized and directed to give any such approval, consent, direction, notice, order,
request, or other action and to execute such documents and take any such action which
such Authorized Officer may deem necessary or desirable to further the purposes of this
Resolution.

  Section 5. All actions heretofore taken by the officers, employees and agents of
the Authority with respect to the issuance and sale of the Bonds are hereby ratified,
confirmed and approved. The officers, employees and agents of the Authority are hereby
authorized and directed, jointly and severally, for and in the name and on behalf of the
Authority, to do any and all things and to take any and all actions and to execute and
deliver any and all agreements, certificates and documents, including, without limitation,
any tax certificates or agreements, bond insurance policies, reserve fund surety policies,
any agreements for depository services, and any agreements for rebate compliance
services, which they, or any of them, may deem necessary or advisable in connection
with the issuance and sale of the Bonds and otherwise to carry out, give effect to and
comply with the terms and intent of the Act, the Measure R Ordinance, the Measure M
Ordinance, this Resolution, the Bonds and the documents approved hereby.

  Section 6.  The effective date of this Resolution shall be the date of its adoption.

  Section 7. The President, or presiding officer, is hereby authorized to affix her
signature to this Resolution signifying its adoption by the Norwalk Community Facilities
Financing Authority and the Secretary, or her duly appointed assistant, is directed to attest
thereto.
